ledger.claim: The rider answered the driver's own 'where are you' message inside the waiting window — 'coming down now', sent 20:51:45 and read by the driver at 20:52:15, only 10 seconds before the free waiting period expired — and the driver then neither posted a reply within 120 seconds of that message nor placed any in-app voice call before terminating the trip at 20:56:19; trip_record.in_app_calls is empty and the silence after the rider's message runs 274 seconds. Limbs (a) and (b) of POL-NS-04 are satisfied on this record: the rider was locating and coordinating, and the failed pickup was at least in part a driver-side coordination failure rather than a rider who ignored the driver. I do not contend the clause exonerates the rider of itself — limb (c) is a separate rider-position test that reads the rider track, and I address that question on its own footing below — but the driver's unbroken silence is a real defect in treating this as a clean rider no-show.

Chargeability under POL-NS-01 is fixed by the driver's conduct alone: an 'arrived' event (limb (a)), qualifying in-geofence fixes (limb (b)), a continuous hold inside the geofence of at least the free waiting period in force (limb (c)) and a termination coded RIDER_NO_SHOW at or after that hold elapsed (limb (d)); POL-NS-06 likewise refunds the fee 'whether or not the rider was present'. The rider's own position is therefore not an element of the charge, and the rider track's 773 m reading cannot be used to make good anything the driver's own evidence leaves out — this fee stands or falls on EV-TRIP-03307 and EV-GPS-03307, and nothing about where the rider's phone was can convert a defective driver case into a good one.

ledger.claim: Two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on rider presence, and that conflict is what should put this case in front of a person. The chat log records the rider telling the driver at 20:51:45 that he is 'coming down now' (EV-CHAT-03307, weight 1.0), while the rider's own track in the same 10-second-cadence trace shows a device that never moved at all across the entire window — 63 fixes from 20:48:06 to 20:57:24, every distinct speed 0.0 km/h — and that never came inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius, its closest approach being 773 m from the pin (EV-GPS-03307, weight 1.0). No clause resolves which of the two is right: POL-NS-04 limb (c) is an exoneration test that reads the rider track and declines to exonerate; it is not a finding about whether a phone motionless for nine minutes was measuring the rider at all, and it leaves that question open. Where two admissible artifacts contradict each other directly on rider presence and no clause settles the conflict, the case goes to a human reviewer under POL-NS-09, and under POL-GEN-03 an escalation holds the disputed $4.50 rather than collecting it — so the rider does not fund a no-show finding while the reliability of the only rider-position record is unresolved.

POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (d) are established on the trip record: the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 20:49:25 (a recorded driver 'arrived' event), no boarding event appears anywhere on the trip, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 20:56:19 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — that is, after the required dwell had elapsed. Both limbs are on the face of the record, not inferred.

POL-NS-01 limb (b) and POL-NS-02 are satisfied by the driver's own trace: 42 qualifying fixes (out of 92) place the driver continuously inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius in a single unbroken in-geofence run from 20:49:25 to 20:56:15, the run beginning exactly at the arrival event. There is no scattered or low-accuracy in-radius reading to attack — the qualification run is continuous.

POL-NS-01 limb (c) is met with a wide margin. The continuous in-geofence dwell measured from the first qualifying fix at 20:49:25 is 410 seconds, against a free waiting period in force of 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec, no_show_threshold_sec being null). The same 410 seconds also clears the 300 second STANDARD dwell figure in the fee schedule, so the outcome does not turn on which minimum is applied.

POL-NS-05 is not engaged and no recomputation of the waiting clock is needed. The 'arrived' marker at 20:49:25 coincides exactly with the first qualifying in-geofence fix, the dwell start offset is 0.0 seconds, and the driver's closest recorded approach to the pin was 0.25 m. The marker was therefore not false: the driver was not more than 300 m away and was not travelling at or above 15 km/h when he tapped.

There is no waiting-period shortfall under POL-NS-06. The measured effective dwell of 410 seconds against the 180 second minimum produces a surplus of 230 seconds (shortfall_sec -230), not a deficit. POL-NS-06 is a rider-exonerating route and it does not bite on these facts.

The POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route is unavailable because EV-ADVIS-03307-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT): assertive reliance on a MISSING traffic_advisory is not open to anyone. I do not rely on it, and the driver does not need it — his dwell is a single continuous in-geofence run, not two intervals to be summed.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. Limb (b) is technically met — the driver did not post a reply within 120 seconds of the rider's 20:51:45 message and logged no in-app call — but limb (c) is affirmatively failed: the rider's own track records 0 qualifying fixes inside the 100 m STANDARD rider-presence radius, its nearest fix being about 773 m from the pin. The clause requires all three limbs conjunctively, so it does not apply and cannot return the fee.

POL-NS-11 confirms the same result even on the reading most generous to the rider: where the rider-presence test cannot be run, POL-NS-04 cannot help the rider and the dispute is decided under the remaining clauses on the driver's own evidence. Here the test can be run and the rider fails it outright, so the fee is decided on the driver's arrival and dwell.

POL-NS-03 does not apply. That clause governs a driver stationary outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin (the wrong-entrance/wrong-block case). The driver here held position inside the 50 m STANDARD radius throughout the qualifying run, so the wrong-entrance route — and its goodwill payment — is not the route this case travels.

The chat log shows the driver performed his side of the coordination. He messaged at 20:49:50 that he was at the pickup point, the rider replied 'coming down now' only at 20:51:45, and the driver then held position a further 4 minutes 29 seconds before cancelling at 20:56:19. Nothing in the log contains the rider naming a different entrance, block or tower that the driver failed to move to.

The rider's own account — 'I was only a few minutes late' — is contradicted by the record. The driver waited a total of about 6.9 minutes (a 410 second qualifying dwell, triggered after a 180 second free waiting period that had already expired), and the rider's device registered no presence within 100 m of the pin at any point in the window. The waiting period the rider paid for was served.

With POL-NS-01 satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displacing it, POL-NS-07 fixes the driver's payout at 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force: 0.80 × SGD 4.50 = SGD 3.60, read from the net figure, which the fare breakdown independently states as driver_compensation of SGD 3.60. The residual 20 percent is the platform service fee.

The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check passes on the citable trailing-window fields: no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the absolute threshold of 4, so the accompanying rate test against completed_trips_30d cannot trip either and compensation is not withheld. No profile field outside the nine the policy names is relied on for this or any other point.

No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is present, so the case is ripe for a monetary ruling. There is no POL-NS-09(b) contradiction — the trip record and the trace agree to the second on arrival (20:49:25) and dwell. Both disputes_with_counterparty_90d counters are 0, the anti-farming check is clear, rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below the 3 that limb (d) reads), and every artifact carrying a deciding fact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so limb (e) is not reached.

There is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and no impairment to discount. The cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.50 equals the net figure produced by the resolution rule (platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd 4.50, within the permitted net-or-gross range), the ledger reconciles to total_charged, and the trace shows 100.0% coverage with no gaps, so all deciding facts rest on weight-1.0 artifacts.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: the fee stands, and here is why. The driver marked himself arrived at 20:49:25 and the platform's own trace shows him inside the 50 m pickup radius in one continuous run of 42 position fixes from 20:49:25 to 20:56:15 — 410 seconds of waiting, measured from the first in-geofence fix and not from the tap (EV-GPS-03307, EV-TRIP-03307). The waiting period this trip allowed was 180 seconds (platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so he held position 230 seconds longer than required before cancelling at 20:56:19 under the code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding recorded. That satisfies all four conditions of POL-NS-01, so the $4.50 cancellation fee was chargeable — that is platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd, and the fare-breakdown line shows the same $4.50. None of the rider-side routes bite: POL-NS-06 needs a shortfall and there is a surplus of 230 seconds; POL-NS-05 needs a false arrival marker and the marker coincided exactly with the first in-geofence fix (dwell start offset 0.0 s, closest approach 0.25 m); POL-NS-03 concerns a driver stationary outside the radius, and this driver was inside it.

You are right that you answered the driver's 'where are you' with 'coming down now' at 20:51:45, and that the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor logged an in-app call — those are limbs (a) and (b) of POL-NS-04. But that clause requires all three of its limbs, and its third reads your own device's track, which placed you about 773 m from the pin on every fix, with no qualifying fix inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius (EV-GPS-03307). So POL-NS-04 does not exonerate you. It would make no difference if that test could not be run at all: POL-NS-11 says the clause then simply cannot help the rider, and the fee is decided on the driver's evidence. Your point that the chat message and the rider track pull in different directions does not send this to a human reviewer. Where your presence matters, the policy names the test that decides it (POL-NS-04(c), and POL-NS-11 if it cannot be run), and the fee itself does not depend on your presence — POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-06 both operate 'whether or not the rider was present'. A clause therefore resolves the point, so the POL-NS-09(b) trigger is not engaged, and no other POL-NS-09 trigger is present: both counterparty-dispute counters are 0, your no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (the limb reads 3), the anti-farming check is clear, and every artifact carrying a deciding fact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so limb (e) is not reached. The disputed fee is not held.

To the driver: POL-NS-07 fixes your payout at 80 percent of the net cancellation fee in force — 0.80 × $4.50 = $3.60, which is also the figure stated on the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-03307). The anti-farming check does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 0 against the absolute threshold of 4, so the accompanying rate test cannot bite either.

No artifact is impaired for policy purposes under POL-NS-08: the arrival event and the nearest trace fix agree to the second, the trace has no gaps and 100 percent coverage, the chat log holds the 2 messages the trip record records, and the cancellation-fee line reconciles with the figure the resolution rule produces. The only missing artifact, the traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-03307-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), is not relied on for any finding, and the single continuous in-geofence run means no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was ever needed. Confidence is 0.90, against a cap of 1.0 set by the weight-1.0 artifacts the finding rests on. The money moved (SGD 3.60) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold. Ruling: DRIVER_COMPENSATION — the $4.50 charge stands and the platform pays the driver $3.60.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
